# Executive Commentary: Budget vs Actual and Rolling Forecast

## Overview

Performance over the period shows a mix of well-understood project timing effects, one confirmed cost overrun on a major Brand Events launch, and a small number of items still under investigation. The rolling forecast for Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) points to net billings of roughly EUR22.61 million and a modest operating result of about EUR247,800 over the three months, with a soft patch expected in August. None of this reflects a deteriorating trend; the largest unfavorable item is a single, well-documented project event, and several favorable variances of similar scale offset it.

## Variance Highlights

The largest item in the period is a confirmed cost overrun on Brand Events' cost of sales, April-June 2025, running roughly EUR1.64 million (+14.2%) above budget. This is corroborated by the business notes log: the Falcon product-launch event in Riyadh saw a major client-driven scope expansion during build week, pushing overtime, staging and freight costs to premium rates. The BU Controller confirmed the overrun at quarter close, with only partial recovery secured through a change order.

A related, smaller episode shows up in April 2026: Brand Events booked an unplanned late-won project delivered on short notice, adding roughly EUR457,000 to cost of sales (+12.0%) and, on the matching revenue line, roughly EUR389,000 of favorable net billings (+8.3%). Per the analyst's review, the net margin impact was slightly negative, and change-order discipline has been flagged to the project director.

On the favorable side, Brand Events also delivered genuine savings of roughly EUR347,000 in cost of sales in November 2024 (per the analyst, in-house crew and staging stock replaced budgeted subcontracting, plus renegotiated Q4 freight) and a timing-driven revenue pull-forward of roughly EUR247,000 in July 2025 (a client roadshow moved from September into July). Corporate Events saw a similar paired timing effect in October 2024, with a brand activation pulled forward adding roughly EUR216,000 to net billings and a matching roughly EUR213,000 to cost of sales.

Digital/Influence had a documented FX-driven shortfall of roughly EUR197,000 in net billings in September 2025 (per the notes log, the euro strengthened against the dollar on a USD-denominated US client contract, with no change in delivered scope). A January 2025 revenue slip of roughly EUR225,000, tied to two platform go-lives delayed into February, was matched by a favorable cost of sales variance of roughly EUR162,000 the same month for the same reason.

Government & Institutions showed several timing-related items in October 2024 (milestone invoicing and matching costs pushed into November) and a one-off IT cost spike of roughly EUR24,100 in November 2024, corroborated by notes describing an emergency hardware and licensing response to an AV system failure during a ministry summit, with an insurance claim filed.

A sustained and favorable episode is worth flagging: Corporate Events' marketing opex ran roughly EUR81,500 (-16.4%) under budget from April 2025 through February 2026, corroborated by notes describing the in-housing of media buying and content creation from July 2025, which management expected to keep spend 20-30% under plan.

One data quality issue was also identified: a Brand Events net billings figure for November 2025 was flagged as a suspected data entry error (actual far exceeding a plausible multiple of budget) and has been excluded from analysis pending correction at source.

## Items Requiring Follow-Up

Two material variances remain unexplained and stay on the follow-up list rather than being attributed a cause. Digital/Influence net billings ran roughly EUR135,000 favorable in August 2025 (+10.2%), and Government & Institutions cost of sales ran roughly EUR68,600 unfavorable in September 2025 (+11.6%). Both should be raised with the respective BU controllers.

## Rolling Forecast

The Q3 2026 forecast projects net billings of roughly EUR22.61 million, cost of sales of roughly EUR16.93 million, and gross margin of roughly EUR5.69 million, with operating result of roughly EUR247,800 for the quarter, equivalent to about 1.1% of net billings. August is expected to be the weakest month, with operating result dipping to roughly -EUR392,000 before recovering in September.

Two methodology points are worth flagging. First, the forecast strips out one-off variances and concluded episodes from the historical base, including the Falcon launch overrun, the pulled-forward projects, and the concluded Corporate Events marketing underspend, so none of those effects are carried into the outlook; this keeps the projection focused on the underlying run rate rather than repeating past anomalies. Second, no sustained programme was still active at the June 2026 cutoff, so no episode effect flows into this forecast.

Overall, the underlying business shows steady growth against prior year across all three business units, with the softer August figure reflecting normal seasonal shape rather than a new concern.
